summary: Scammers in West Africa and Morocco used AI-generated photos and fake military profiles to run romance scams on US widows and other vulnerable people, building trust before asking for money. Some victims lost their life savings.
technical_summary: Generative image tools produce realistic photos of soldiers, with medals and uniforms, to support fabricated personas on social media and dating sites. The AI imagery makes the romance scam more convincing and harder to detect, enabling long-running emotional manipulation and untraceable payments.

summary: Facebook pages posted AI-generated false stories about an Australian football club and its players, including fake arrests and criminal allegations. The club asked Meta to act, and some pages were later removed.
technical_summary: Pages used generative AI text and images to produce repeated, similar false stories presented as news, often with vague teasers and suspicious links. Cross-posting among pages amplified the content, and platform detection and removal were slow and partial.

summary: Amazon's Choice badge, which recommends products partly by star ratings, was shown on products with faulty quality and with recycled or purchased reviews. Amazon was reported as unable to stop the review manipulation.
technical_summary: A ranking and badge system relied on star scores that could be gamed through review recycling, bought reviews and replacement offers that changed ratings. As a result, defective products received badges, and shoppers had a harder time telling good products from bad.

technology.quote: Recommending products based on their star score comes with other complications, too

failure_mode.quote: is Amazon unable to crack down on bad actors

affected_population.quote: they do make it harder for shoppers to distinguish legitimately good products from crappy ones

summary: Brazilian police arrested suspects accused of running Instagram ads with deepfakes of a famous model and other celebrities to promote fake giveaways and products. The scheme reportedly moved over 20 million reais, mostly from small losses that went unreported.
technical_summary: Deepfake videos of celebrities were used in social media ads to sell nonexistent products and collect shipping fees, then funds were laundered. Small per-victim losses and low reporting let the operation scale, while platform ad screening did not catch the celebrity-bait ads.

technical_summary: A news outlet used an AI chatbot to paraphrase articles at scale with little human editing. An error attached a real person's photo to a story about someone else, and a portal syndicated it. High-volume automated publishing produced repeated falsehoods without effective review.

summary: Italy's data protection authority temporarily banned ChatGPT, citing the lack of a legal basis for mass collection of personal data to train it, a data breach, inaccurate data and no age checks. OpenAI restored service in Italy after making changes.
technical_summary: The regulator found that large-scale training data collection lacked a legal basis under the GDPR, that a breach exposed users' conversations and payment details, and that no age verification protected minors. OpenAI blocked access in Italy, then added age checks, opt-out forms and clearer privacy notices.

summary: NBC News found that a simple publicly known jailbreak prompt could make several OpenAI models give detailed instructions for explosives, chemical agents, biological weapons and nuclear bombs. OpenAI had not fixed it in several tested models.
technical_summary: Safety guardrails on four OpenAI models, two of them usable in ChatGPT, were bypassed with a short jailbreak prompt, producing hundreds of hazardous responses. Competing models declined the same requests. The finding was a red-team test; no real-world harm was reported.

technology.quote: NBC News was able to generate hundreds of responses with instructions on how to create homemade explosives

failure_mode.quote: a series of words that any user can send to a chatbot to bypass its security rules

notes: Potential risk shown by journalist testing; no misuse reported.

summary: A hospital's AI sepsis alert led staff to order IV fluids for an elderly patient with a dialysis catheter, which could have overloaded her system. A nurse objected and a physician ordered a different treatment instead.
technical_summary: A sepsis prediction flag in the hospital's electronic system triggered a standard protocol of rapid fluids without accounting for the patient's kidney condition. The alert created pressure to comply over bedside clinical judgment. A physician overrode it, averting harm.

notes: Single-nurse account; the hospital could not comment on the specific case.

summary: Artists accused the text-to-image model Stable Diffusion, and apps built on it such as Lensa, of using their artwork for training without permission and undercutting their work by selling cheap AI portraits.
